clue.text: Tips from writer with daughter in America

indicators.note: in places the writer and daughter inside the letters for America

parts.note: a pen is a thing that writes
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An author living in the States with their daughter passes on some advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' reads as a noun, pieces of advice, but here it is a verb: tips something over.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: someone who tips a thing over turns it on its end.

clue.text: One supplying plug for engine you can pick up?

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the phrase is taken by ear

parts.note: pro means for, and a motor is an engine, giving the spoken phrase pro motor

explanation.surface: Somebody who sells spark plugs for an engine that you can collect.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'plug' is a piece of publicity, not a spark plug. 'For engine' becomes 'pro motor', which 'you can pick up' tells us to hear rather than read.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a favourable mention, and the person who provides such publicity is one who pushes an event or product.

clue.text: Rubbish won't burn in the shade

indicators.note: rubbish is a mess, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Garden waste left out of the sun refuses to catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' asks for the letters of WONT BURN to be rearranged; 'in the' merely joins. The shade is a colour, not shelter from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a rich dark colour, the hue of a ripe hazelnut.

clue.text: Raised a large cover over father's tree

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means everything that follows is written upwards

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a lid is a cover
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
pa is father, so father's is pa's

explanation.surface: Someone lifted a big sheet to protect Dad's tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns the whole run A, L, LID, O, PAS upside down in this down clue, giving the tropical American tree whose latex is chicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a tropical American evergreen, the source of chicle.

clue.text: Say nothing about preference for nagging

parts.note: sh! is an instruction to say nothing
re means about or concerning
a wish is a desire or preference

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about your liking for constant complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as an adjective: both describe a bad-tempered, scolding person.

clue.text: Earmark hypermarket, perhaps, to give huge value

definitions.meaning: read literally and playfully: to put aside (earmark) a very large shop
the idiom meaning to regard something as very important

explanation.surface: Pick out a giant supermarket that offers terrific bargains.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading: a hypermarket is a very big shop, and to earmark one is to put it aside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for valuing something highly, which read word by word could describe reserving an enormous shop.

clue.text: Use a lot of each colour filling in box

parts.note: ea is the commercial abbreviation for each
a tint is a colour

indicators.note: the filling of a word is what sits in its middle, here one central letter

explanation.surface: Get through plenty of every crayon while shading a square.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal synonym: to consume a large part of something, as costs do to savings.

clue.text: Home, compact in size, for the richer

parts.note: in means at home
pocket as an adjective means small, as with a pocket dictionary

explanation.surface: A small house, suitable for wealthier people.
explanation.walkthrough: After a sum of money both phrases mean the same: ten pounds the richer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: having made a gain, said after an amount of money.

clue.text: Chap managed to collect medal for serving livestock owner

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a chap

indicators.note: to collect is to take in, so managed gathers the medal inside itself

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
DSM is the Distinguished Service Medal, a military decoration

explanation.surface: A man succeeded in picking up a decoration for his work for a farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for serving' belongs to the medal, the Distinguished Service Medal, which 'to collect' places inside; it is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: a person who keeps or tends a group of cattle or sheep.

clue.text: Weakness that's not hard to see

parts.note: soft is the opposite of hard
to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: A flaw that is easy to notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard to see' reads as 'easy to notice', but it splits: not hard, then see.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of a fondness: having a weakness for something is being partial to it.

clue.text: Being out of place in harbour, finally sailor returned

indicators.note: returned means the whole assembled run comes back the other way
finally takes the closing letter of the word before it
in sets the word for place inside the pieces that follow it

parts.note: OS is ordinary seaman, a naval rank
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A seaman who was in the wrong spot in port has at last come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being out' is being unconscious, not being abroad. 'in' and 'finally' build ROPUTS, which 'returned' then turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of near-unconsciousness, which is what being out cold amounts to.

clue.text: Transport add-on, one given to appropriate vehicles?

parts.note: transport as a noun is rapture or great delight
a rider is a clause added to a document

explanation.surface: An accessory for a car, bestowed on suitable vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' is a verb here, to take without permission, and 'given to' means inclined to.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who habitually steals cars to drive them for fun.

clue.text: Reverses and runs down

definitions.meaning: as a noun, setbacks or blows of misfortune
as a verb, criticises or disparages

explanation.definitionFit: Both a plural noun for setbacks and a verb for disparaging; life's blows and what a critic does.

clue.text: Aussie skipper adding a run to total in chase

indicators.note: in places the total, a and run inside the word for chase

parts.note: to woo is to pursue or chase romantically

indicators.note: adding says a and run are tacked on after the word for total

parts.note: all is the total, the whole lot
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Australia's cricket captain contributes a single to the score while chasing a target.
explanation.walkthrough: The skipper is an animal that skips or hops, not a team captain; 'adding' and 'in' only fix the order of the cricket-flavoured pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hopping marsupial of Australia, so a bounder or jumper from that country.

clue.text: Fido at last caught, dog collar is going on

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the name before it

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a cur is a mongrel dog
a ring is a band round something, as a collar is

explanation.surface: The pet is finally captured and its lead is being attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something happening or taking place.

clue.text: She had pop award reduced

indicators.note: reduced means the word for award is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a grant is a sum of money awarded

explanation.surface: A singer finds the prize for her chart music has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' is father: she is the woman who gave birth to him. 'reduced' drops the last letter of GRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a father's mother: the woman who bore Dad.

clue.text: Person who offers to hold case for cockney traveller

indicators.note: to hold says the person who offers keeps the case inside

parts.note: one who offers something is a giver

indicators.note: a cockney is taken to drop an initial H from a word

parts.note: a hull is the husk or outer case of a seed or fruit

explanation.surface: Somebody volunteers to carry a suitcase for a Londoner on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney, an East Londoner, is said to drop the letter H in speech, which is what 'for cockney' asks of the case before 'to hold' tucks it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Swift's fictional ship's surgeon, famous for his voyages.

clue.text: Maybe tick playing card in a hand, initially

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters move about as in a game

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Perhaps mark off the card you play first from your hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing card' looks like one phrase but splits: 'playing' is the anagram signal, with 'initially' adding H to the mix. The tick is a creature, not a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: ticks belong to the eight-legged class that includes spiders and mites.

clue.text: Boy back in detention at school

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lad is kept in after lessons once again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back in' gives the game away: the letters NATS sit across 'detention at school' and are read from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a male first name, short for Stanley.

clue.text: Outside right, cunningly, apes the fellow top wingers

indicators.note: outside says the reworked word goes round the letter for right
cunningly suggests the letters are craftily rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
him is a pronoun for the fellow

explanation.surface: A footballer on the right flank cleverly copies his team's best wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: The wingers are winged beings, not footballers, and 'Outside right' is no position on the pitch: 'cunningly' makes SEAP, which 'Outside' wraps round the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest order of angels, traditionally shown with six wings.

clue.text: Union spent to bring in a civil engineer

indicators.note: to bring in says the word for spent takes the next letter inside

parts.note: all in means exhausted or spent

explanation.surface: A trade union paid out money to hire a technical expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spent' is exhausted, ALL IN, which 'to bring in' opens for the A; CE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a joining of parties or states for a common purpose.

clue.text: Hiding, maybe, in service area

parts.note: mass is a church service
an acre is a measure of area

explanation.surface: Someone possibly lying low at a motorway stop.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hiding' is a heavy beating or defeat, not concealment; a service area is a British motorway rest stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally both mean a crushing defeat, as in sport.

clue.text: Peel the source of this pus?

definitions.text: Peel the source of this pus?

parts.words: Peel the source of this pus?
parts.note: Peel is a town on the Isle of Man, and pus is puss with its tail cut off, like the island's tailless breed

explanation.walkthrough: Peel is a town on the Isle of Man, and 'pus' is 'puss' without its tail: an animal from that island famous for having none.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailless breed of feline from the island where the town of Peel lies.

clue.text: Moon, mostly, keeps spinning around in space

indicators.note: keeps says the moon word holds the next piece within it
mostly means the word is used without its last letter

parts.note: lunar is the adjective for the moon, as moon landing and lunar landing are the same

indicators.note: spinning turns the short word for around the other way

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around or about

explanation.surface: The Moon goes on turning for most of the time as it circles in the void.
explanation.walkthrough: The space is a gap, not outer space. 'mostly' leaves LUNA, and 'spinning' makes AC from the abbreviation of circa, which 'keeps' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a gap or missing portion, as in a manuscript.

clue.text: Dispatching letters from un, a minor foreign correspondent?

definitions.note: the question mark allows that the phrase is unfinished, a place name normally following

indicators.note: dispatching the letters sends them off to new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A junior reporter abroad sends mail from the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatching letters from' rearranges UN A MINOR. The result is the stock phrase for a journalist or agent abroad, as in Graham Greene's Our Man in Havana.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase a newspaper uses for its reporter stationed in a named place abroad.

clue.text: Lose track of exceptionally fine port

indicators.note: lose tells us the track is dropped from the phrase that follows

parts.note: very nice is a plain way of saying exceptionally fine
ry is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A drinker forgets how much outstanding fortified wine they have had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose' removes RY (railway) from VERY NICE. The port is a harbour city, not the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an Italian city on the Adriatic with a historic harbour.

clue.text: Revelation in tweet set back husband — and then some!

indicators.note: and then says the last piece follows what has gone before
set back means the word for tweet is written from its end to its start

parts.note: to pipe is to chirp or tweet as a bird does
H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband
any can mean some, as in have you any money

explanation.surface: Something disclosed on social media upset a husband, and more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and then some' looks like the idiom for 'and more besides' but splits into a position phrase and a word for some; 'set back' gives EPIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a sudden moment of insight or disclosure.

clue.text: Austrian count's last letter, dark, yet animated

definitions.note: the possessive is only there for the surface; the answer is the count himself

indicators.note: animated means set in motion, so the letters before it move about

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Austrian nobleman's final note is gloomy but lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animated' rearranges Z, DARK and YET. He was the field marshal for whom Johann Strauss senior wrote a famous march.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a nineteenth-century field marshal and nobleman of the Habsburg empire.

clue.text: Boring article, on golf, they've permitted me

indicators.note: on says the phrase is added on to the letter for golf, following it

parts.note: Golf is the word for G in the NATO phonetic alphabet
if they have permitted me, then I'm let

explanation.surface: They have allowed me to write a tedious magazine piece about golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring article' is a thing that bores holes, not a dull essay. 'they've permitted me' is restated as I'M LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand tool for making holes, so an object that bores.
